item.title: A Hacking Competition Shows the Power of China’s Approach to A.I.
item.description: The winner of a cybersecurity contest prevailed by relying on an ‘open weight’ Chinese model — another sign that available A.I. systems could already be too powerful to easily regulate.
item.dc:creator: Cade Metz
item.media:credit: Avishag Shaar-Yashuv for The New York Times
item.media:description: Pavel Gurvich, the chief executive of the cybersecurity company Tenzai. Mr. Gurvich’s firm won the HackerOne contest by using a freely available Chinese A.I. model.

item.title: Clues to Why a Breakthrough Pancreatic Cancer Drug Eventually Stops Working
item.description: Researchers are asking why patients, like former Senator Ben Sasse, inevitably develop resistance to the drug daraxonrasib.
item.dc:creator: Gina Kolata
item.media:credit: T.J. Kirkpatrick for The New York Times
item.media:description: Researchers are studying why patients, like former Senator Ben Sasse, eventually develop resistance to the drug daraxonrasib.

item.title: Cornell’s Jane Doe Said She Was Given Ketamine. Here’s How the Drug Works.
item.description: Ketamine is a short-acting anesthetic that can have hallucinogenic effects. It is becoming more easily available, and some experts fear misuse is increasing.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Jacobs
item.media:credit: Julie Ezvan/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Ketamine can have a hallucinogenic effect at certain doses.

item.title: New Cancer Drugs Are Revolutionary. Why Don’t More Patients Get Them?
item.description: Targeted gene therapies are highly effective at stopping cancers, but the very abundance of the treatments, plus cost and sluggish change, are hindering access.
item.dc:creator: Gina Kolata
item.media:credit: Emily Elconin for The New York Times
item.media:description: When John Ebers, a commercial beekeeper in Comstock Park, Mich., was diagnosed with Stage 3 colorectal cancer, he was not given the option of genetic testing, which could have revealed if there were drugs that could attack his cancer.

item.title: Ukrainian Science Academy, Struck by Drone, Played Key Role in Research
item.description: Over 90 percent of Ukraine’s scientific discoveries have been attributed to Ukraine’s National Academy of Sciences, including advancements in astronomy and military technology.
item.dc:creator: Robin George Andrews and Nataliia Novosolova
item.media:credit: Finbarr O'Reilly for The New York Times
item.media:description: A Russian drone strike on the National Academy of Sciences in Kyiv, Ukraine, killed at least two people on Monday.

item.title: Radio Waves Coming From an Alien Planet May Be a Cosmic First
item.description: Beta Pictoris b appears to have an aurora caused by a powerful magnetic field. If confirmed, it would be the first such field known outside our solar system.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan O’Callaghan
item.media:credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Ralf Crawford (STScI)
item.media:description: An artist’s concept shows the Beta Pictoris system, which contains three gas giant exoplanets, 63 light-years from Earth.

item.title: What If A.D.H.D. Isn’t About Attention at All?
item.description: Evidence suggests that it really affects what psychiatrists like me call sustained engagement — an important difference in understanding how to think about the condition.
item.dc:creator: Awais Aftab

item.title: Anthropic’s Quest for Humanlike A.I.
item.description: Elizabeth Dias, our national religion correspondent, and Cade Metz, one of our technology reporters, discuss Anthropic’s approach for instilling morality into Claude — which has involved consultations with religious leaders, including ones at the Vatican — and why it’s raising questions.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Dias, Cade Metz, Christina Shaman, Chris Whitworth, Stephanie Swart, Whitney Shefte and Mark Oltmanns

item.title: This Virus Stole a Human Gene and Won’t Let Go of It
item.description: Scientists have found a human gene lurking in a virus that causes skin infections. It may be using our own DNA to infect us.
item.dc:creator: Carl Zimmer
item.media:credit: Science Source
item.media:description: Molluscum contagiosum virus, which causes sores on skin, swiped a gene from humans about 100,000 years ago according to a new study.

item.title: Viper Image That Caused Alarm in California Was A.I.-Generated
item.description: A Gaboon viper, a venomous snake native to equatorial regions of Africa, was supposedly photographed in a tree in Santa Ana, Calif. How could that be? Well, it turns out it wasn’t.
item.dc:creator: Victor Mather
item.media:credit: Joel Saget/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: This is a real Gaboon viper. One that was supposedly photographed in a tree in Santa Ana, Calif., was fake.

item.title: See How El Niño Is Washing Ashore in California
item.description: An enormous pulse of wave energy will soon reach Southern California and continue north, raising sea levels by half a foot and increasing threats from swells and tides.
item.dc:creator: Raymond Zhong
item.media:credit: Mario Tama/Getty Images
item.media:description: A wave crashes into a sea wall protecting beachfront homes in Long Beach, Ca., where a boardwalk was damaged by Hurricane Marie.

item.title: Tennessee Valley Authority Gets Approval to Build Small Nuclear Reactor
item.description: It’s only the second time that American regulators have approved a next-generation commercial reactor for construction. Big hurdles remain.
item.dc:creator: Brad Plumer
item.media:credit: Audra Melton for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Vogtle nuclear plant in Georgia cost $35 billion to build.

item.title: V.A. Institutes New Consent Requirements for Some Psychiatric Drugs
item.description: Veterans under 30 will have to sign forms before being given antidepressants. Medical groups fear the moves may stigmatize mental health treatment.
item.dc:creator: Azeen Ghorayshi and Andrew Jacobs
item.media:credit: Reuters
item.media:description: The new policies will go into effect in 2027.

item.title: Despite Setbacks, NASA Gives Boeing’s Starliner Spacecraft a Boost
item.description: A previous mission left two astronauts stuck in space for months. Still, the space agency is investing $359 million to keep the craft flying.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth Chang
item.media:credit: NASA, via Associated Press
item.media:description: Boeing’s Starliner spacecraft could make another trip to the International Space Station as soon as December, but this time carrying only cargo.

item.title: The Coal Industry Asked for a Rescue. Trump Obliged.
item.description: In a previously unreported letter, a top lobbyist floated the idea of using emergency powers to keep aging coal plants open.
item.dc:creator: Brad Plumer and Claire Brown
item.media:credit: Rachel Woolf for The New York Times
item.media:description: Coal plants were ordered to stay open, including Craig Generating Station in Colorado, which challenged the emergency order.

item.title: Judge Blocks FEMA From Tying Antiterrorism Grants to Election Changes
item.description: The Trump administration had threatened to withhold some Homeland Security money unless states explored paper balloting and citizenship verification.
item.dc:creator: Scott Dance
item.media:credit: Sophie Park for The New York Times
item.media:description: Voters cast primary election ballots in Augusta, Maine, in June. A court ruled Monday that the Trump administration cannot withhold federal terrorism preparedness grants from states and localities that don’t explore shifting to paper ballots.

item.title: Trump Sharply Scales Back Fuel Economy Rules for New Cars
item.description: The move marked the final step in the administration’s efforts to dismantle policies aimed at speeding the shift to electric vehicles.
item.dc:creator: Brad Plumer and Maxine Joselow
item.media:credit: Kenny Holston/The New York Times
item.media:description: The new standards should be relatively easy for automakers to meet, analysts said.

item.title: SpaceX’s Starship Makes It to Orbit for the First Time, but Returns to Earth Early
item.description: The 14th test flight marks a crucial milestone toward the company’s ambitions of sending people to the moon and Mars, but it was not a complete success.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth Chang
item.media:credit: SpaceX, via Reuters

item.title: Did Anthropic’s A.I. Really Make a Scientific Discovery on Its Own?
item.description: An expert at the University of Copenhagen said his team had been sharing its research with the company’s A.I. model, Claude, and that its new finding matched their work.
item.dc:creator: Carl Zimmer
item.media:credit: Jason Henry for The New York Times

item.title: Dogs Will Fight Bears. But Not Because of the Reason You Might Think.
item.description: Scientists analyzed hundreds of encounters between bears and canines. The results raise the suggestion that dogs may not always protect people in the wild.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Nazaryan

item.title: How El Niño Is Shaping Storms on Two Sides of the U.S.
item.description: Hurricanes near Hawaii. A nor’easter on the East Coast. The ocean phenomenon’s influence on storms around the country may just be getting started.
item.dc:creator: Raymond Zhong
item.media:credit: Dave Sanders for The New York Times
item.media:description: Flooding in Point Pleasant Beach, N.J., on Saturday.

item.title: California Needs Water. El Niño Might Bring Too Much to Keep.
item.description: The drought-stricken state has improved its ability to collect and store rainwater. But many gallons may still rush into the Pacific.
item.dc:creator: Scott Dance
item.media:credit: Getty Images
item.media:description: Gov. Gavin Newsom of California has declared a state of emergency to mobilize disaster resources before El Niño peaks.

item.title: ‘Zombified’ C.D.C., Hobbled by Cuts, Struggles to Fulfill Scientific Mission
item.description: The agency has lost its independence and nearly a third of its staff, as Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and associates have tightened control.
item.dc:creator: Apoorva Mandavilli
item.category: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
item.media:credit: Elijah Nouvelage/Getty Images
item.media:description: A protest outside the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention last year after employees were laid off. Beyond staff reductions, the agency also faces a leadership vacuum.

item.title: In an $80 Motel Room, a Discovery to Shed Light on the Origins of Life
item.description: A scrappy science project led to a significant discovery: two new species of a rare organism that could elucidate a fundamental transition in the history of life on our planet.
item.dc:creator: Carolyn Y. Johnson

item.title: Four Beluga Whales Die Weeks After Major Rescue Mission
item.description: The belugas were among 30 whales transferred to aquariums in the United States and Spain from a closed marine attraction in Canada.
item.dc:creator: Remy Tumin
item.media:credit: Rachel Mittelstaedt/Shedd Aquarium, via Associated Press
item.media:description: A beluga whale named Osiris at the Shedd Aquarium in Chicago in August. It was one of four belugas to die after being transferred from a closed marine park in Canada.

item.title: Byron Sher, Early Environmental Warrior in California, Dies at 98
item.description: A congenial legislator with a professorial air, he won battles through charm, not pugilism, passing laws to protect drinking water, redwood forests and clean air.
item.dc:creator: Trip Gabriel

item.title: Is China Really Stealing A.I. From American Companies?
item.description: As Xi Jinping visits President Trump in Washington, the leaders are expected to discuss claims that China is surreptitiously copying American A.I. technologies, a process known as distillation.
item.dc:creator: Cade Metz
item.media:credit: Hector Retamal/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: The Chinese companies Z.ai and Moonshot are not far behind Anthropic and OpenAI.

item.title: On This Mexican Island, Raccoons Make and Play With Toys (and Also Sip Margaritas)
item.description: Scientists observed a family of pygmy raccoons near a Cozumel beach club learning from one another how to craft balls from paper, an indication that the animals have a culture.
item.dc:creator: Taylor Mitchell Brown

item.title: In a New Anthropic Lab, A.I. Turns to Biology
item.description: Scientists at the company announced their first finding: a group of enzymes whose function is unknown.
item.dc:creator: Carl Zimmer
item.media:credit: Jason Henry/Bloomberg
item.media:description: Anthropic’s San Francisco headquarters.

item.title: A Second Judge Strikes Down New York’s Climate ‘Superfund’ Law
item.description: A federal judge ruled that the new law, which would force fossil fuel companies to pay $75 billion to help cover the costs of climate change, was unconstitutional.
item.dc:creator: Karen Zraick
item.media:credit: Libby March for The New York Times
item.media:description: The plant in Somerset, N.Y., which closed in 2020, was the last coal-fired power station in the state.
